rationale: Evidence. Iteration 6 already raced base_speed 1.25 (with ki 0, kd 0.15, last_direction, x = +/-0.03 with 16 mm footprints). Its max_error was 0.0606, 0.0653 and 0.0657 m, against 0.0607, 0.0648 and 0.0621 at 1.4, so speed made no measurable difference to the excursion. Every design so far has ended off track on all 60 trials with exactly one line-loss event per trial. Progress was 0.11 to 0.165 and there were no completions. The Evaluator's authorised feedback for this candidate was written as if 1.25 had not yet raced, but the race data shows it has, so its guidance (a) does not apply. Its guidance (b) does apply: max_error and line-loss count are unchanged, so speed is not the limit. Following that guidance, I restore base_speed to 1.4 and make one controller change: kp from 1.5 to 2.0, with kd 0.15, ki 0 and last_direction unchanged. The fixed-bias (ki), damping (kd), recovery-direction (line_loss) and speed hypotheses have each been tested with no effect on the 0.060 to 0.065 m excursion. Stiffer proportional steering is the one controller variable not yet isolated, and the robot is drifting toward the line edge before the first loss. Expected result: max_error falls to 0.06 m or below on some seeds, or line-loss events drop, and progress is at least unchanged. The risk is that kp 2.0 with kd 0.15 adds oscillation (steering_oscillation rising sharply with no gain). I am not changing geometry: widening the sensors to +/-0.05 previously cut progress, and the off-track limit cannot be raised with body_width. Measurements wanted: max_error and line_loss_events per track to test whether stiffer steering holds the line; steering_oscillation to check for jitter; progress and completion_time to see whether the run gets further; completion to check for any finish. If max_error is still about 0.060 to 0.065 m with one loss per trial, the next step is to add sensor spacing or footprint changes at the outer sensors, not further gain tuning.
